title: Tuning Density and Spin Ordering of Degenerate Fermi Gases in an Optical Cavity
authors: Wei Qin, Yuan-Hong Chen, Renyuan Liao
abstract: We investigate a spin-degenerate Fermi gas coupled to a high-finesse optical cavity, where the competition between scalar and vectorial couplings is controlled by the relative polarization angle of the pump and cavity fields. We find that the phase transition threshold is synergistically determined by the scalar-vectorial coupling weight and Pauli blocking, with the latter dictating the critical pump lattice depth required for the onset of superradiance. For a two-component Fermi gas with opposite spins, the population ratio drives two distinct types of phase transitions corresponding to real-space phase separation: continuous and discontinuous. Nevertheless, the boundary of the phase transition remains fundamentally governed by the scalar-vectorial coupling competition. We clarify the impact of the relative polarization angle on phase transitions of the system; these results also apply to bosonic systems. Our results provide valuable theoretical insights for future experimental realizations.
summary: This theoretical study explores superradiant phase transitions in Fermi gases coupled to optical cavities, demonstrating that the transition point is controlled by a competition between scalar and vectorial light-matter couplings. By tuning the relative polarization angle of the driving fields, researchers can manipulate this coupling balance, leading to insights applicable to both fermionic and bosonic quantum systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the superradiant quantum phase transition (QPT) occurring in a spin-degenerate Fermi gas coupled to an optical cavity.
main_result: The phase transition threshold is found to be synergistically determined by both the scalar-vectorial coupling weight and Pauli blocking effects. Furthermore, the relative polarization angle can tune the competition between these couplings.
method: The analysis employs mean-field theory applied to the effective Hamiltonian derived after eliminating excited states, utilizing steady-state solutions of the Lindblad master equation and free energy minimization techniques.
model_or_system: The system is a spin-degenerate Fermi gas confined in a high-finesse optical cavity, where interactions are mediated by light fields whose coupling strength depends on the relative polarization angle ($\phi$) between the pump and cavity fields. The model incorporates both scalar and vectorial atom-light couplings.

paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the effective Hamiltonian, deriving mean-field equations for photon dynamics, analyzing the conditions for superradiance via free energy minimization, and finally mapping out complex phase diagrams showing how polarization angle and density control the transition order and type.
why_interesting: This work bridges concepts from cavity QED (superradiance) with strongly interacting quantum matter (Fermi gases), providing tunable control over collective quantum phenomena using light polarization—a highly relevant area for experimental AMO physics.
